subject: On-prem edge latency — request to attribute/except customer-managed routing
messages:
From: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien.dupont@aretebio.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gregor Hsu <gregor.hsu@aretebio.com>, Arete Bio Network Ops <netops@aretebio.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Observed spikes impacting egress latency — asking for attribution guidance

Hi Soojin,

We observed recurring 200–600ms outbound latency spikes to Redwood-hosted Private endpoints on 2026-11-06 between 01:02–01:26 UTC. Our on-prem edge team has pulled router logs and traceroutes; attaching the first set for your review.

Before we escalate formally with procurement/legal, can Redwood confirm whether these events would fall within Redwood's SLA scope for our Private deployment? Our edge is customer-controlled (BGP-speaking NAT gateway + dual ISPs) and we suspect transient BGP path flaps and asymmetric routing are the cause.

We'd appreciate guidance on evidence you need to accept network-exclusion attribution (e.g., specific packet captures, BGP RIB screenshots, timestamped traceroutes). If needed we'll open a NetOps ticket and can coordinate a short debug window.

Thanks — Aurelien

Attachment: edge_router_logs_20261106.txt (text/plain, 128KB)
Attachment: traceroute_samples_11-06.pdf (application/pdf, 230KB)

Aurelien Dupont
Head of Infra, Arete Bio
aurelien.dupont@aretebio.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien.dupont@aretebio.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observed spikes impacting egress latency — asking for attribution guidance

Hi Aurelien,

Thanks for the logs — useful. Short answer: we can accept a customer-network exclusion in the Private deployment SLA when the evidence shows the fault originates from customer-managed edge (BGP/peering/ISP). We have a lightweight evidence checklist and an addendum template we use for carveouts.

What we need initially from your side:
- Time-windowed traceroutes with consistent timestamps across multiple vantage points (you already included a sample, thanks)
- BGP RIB snapshots from the edge showing route changes + timestamps
- Router syslog excerpts around the spike window (interface flaps, BGP events)
- Flow-level counters showing increased retransmits/queueing (if available)

If those artifacts show the fault on Arete's edge, Redwood will:
1) Classify the incident as "customer-managed network" for the purpose of SLA attribution, and
2) Propose a short addendum (1–2 clauses) carving out that time range from availability/latency SLO calculations for this Private deployment.

I've looped in Kar and Dylan for legal/ops review. I'd like to propose a 30-minute troubleshooting window tomorrow 09:00–09:30 PT with NetOps on both sides to capture live traces if you can.

Best,

— Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Attachment: proposed-carveout-addendum.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 18KB)

From: Gregor Hsu <gregor.hsu@aretebio.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien.dupont@aretebio.com>, netops@aretebio.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observed spikes impacting egress latency — asking for attribution guidance

Soojin — thanks. We can provide the BGP RIB snapshots and full syslog extracts. The team prefers the troubleshooting window tomorrow at 09:00 PT; Gregor (netops lead) will be on the call and will also share a live BGP session dump.

One quick question: how granular is the carveout? Are you able to exclude only the exact minute ranges proven to be customer-side faults, or does Redwood require whole maintenance windows to be carved out? We want the minimum carveout possible.

— Gregor
Network Operations Lead, Arete Bio
netops@aretebio.com

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Gregor Hsu <gregor.hsu@aretebio.com>, Aurelien Dupont <aurelien.dupont@aretebio.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observed spikes impacting egress latency — asking for attribution guidance

Gregor/Aurelien — great sync earlier; appreciate the detailed traces. Summary + next steps below.

Summary of findings (Redwood runtime ops + Arete netops):
- Multiple transient BGP withdraws observed at 01:05:21–01:06:03 UTC correlated with increased RTT and packet reordering.
- Arete-side interface counters show significant output drops on AS64521:eth0 at 01:05:20 UTC.
- No evidence of tokenization or model runtime backpressure on Redwood side during the window; internal tracing shows normal request processing latency.

Action items:
1) Redwood Ops will accept a minute-range exclusion for 01:05:20–01:06:10 UTC on 2026-11-06, to be applied to Arete's Private deployment availability calculations.
2) Legal/Contracts: Kar (karthik_iyer) will review the wording and push an addendum via DocuSign for an SLA carveout clause that references the precise timestamps and artifacts.
3) Operational runbook: Dylan will draft a 1-page joint runbook for future incidents (contact points, evidence checklist, and mitigation playbook).

Please confirm you want us to proceed with the DocuSign addendum and we'll route it to your signatory. Once signed, the carveout will be applied retroactively to the 2026-11-06 incident and noted in Redwood's incident ledger.

Thanks — Soojin

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 15:50 Gregor Hsu <gregor.hsu@aretebio.com> wrote:
> Confirm — please send the DocuSign to legal@aretebio.com and cc netops@aretebio.com. We'll review and aim to sign within 48 hours.
>
> — Gregor
